prompt: America Online launched under the AOL name
explanation: AOL helped turn going online into a mainstream household activity in the 1990s, complete with dial-up tones and free trial discs.

prompt: The Trojan Room coffee pot became one of the first famous webcams
explanation: Cambridge researchers pointed a camera at a coffee pot so colleagues could check whether coffee was available without walking down the hall.

prompt: Pizza Hut took an early pizza order over the web
explanation: PizzaNet became an early symbol of something that once sounded absurd: ordering dinner through a web browser.

prompt: JavaScript was created for the Netscape browser
explanation: Brendan Eich created the language that would become essential to interactive web pages and modern web apps.

prompt: The original Space Jam website went online
explanation: The movie site became a beloved time capsule of 1990s web design and remained online for decades.

prompt: AOL Instant Messenger launched
explanation: AIM made buddy lists, away messages and screen names part of everyday online life for a generation.

prompt: Google published its first Doodle
explanation: The first Doodle referenced Burning Man and started a tradition of changing the Google logo for events, people and anniversaries.

prompt: MSN Messenger launched
explanation: Messenger became one of the defining chat apps of the early 2000s, especially for teens and students.

prompt: LiveJournal launched
explanation: LiveJournal blended personal blogging with friends, comments and communities before social networks became mainstream.

prompt: Habbo Hotel opened its virtual hotel
explanation: Habbo mixed chat rooms, avatars and virtual furniture years before metaverse became a buzzword.

prompt: Apple launched iTunes
explanation: iTunes became a central tool for organizing digital music before the iTunes Store arrived two years later.

prompt: Xbox Live launched
explanation: Xbox Live helped normalize console gaming with persistent online identities, friends lists and multiplayer matchmaking.

prompt: LinkedIn launched
explanation: LinkedIn brought professional identity and networking into the social-web era.

prompt: Flickr launched
explanation: Flickr helped popularize photo sharing, tags and online communities built around photography.

prompt: World of Warcraft launched
explanation: World of Warcraft turned the massively multiplayer online world into a mainstream cultural phenomenon.

prompt: Etsy launched its marketplace for handmade goods
explanation: Etsy built a major online marketplace around independent makers, crafts and vintage goods.

prompt: Facebook introduced the News Feed
explanation: The News Feed shifted social networking from visiting profiles to scrolling a constantly updated stream of activity.

prompt: Nintendo released the Wii
explanation: The Wii brought motion controls into living rooms and attracted many people who did not think of themselves as gamers.

prompt: Netflix started streaming movies and TV shows online
explanation: Netflix began moving beyond DVDs by letting subscribers watch video instantly on their computers.

prompt: Rickrolling became an Internet bait-and-switch phenomenon
explanation: Links promising something else began redirecting people to Rick Astley’s Never Gonna Give You Up, creating one of the web’s most durable jokes.

prompt: Spotify launched its music streaming service
explanation: Spotify’s launch helped accelerate the shift from owning music files to streaming huge catalogs on demand.

prompt: Facebook introduced the Like button
explanation: A tiny thumbs-up button became one of the most recognizable interaction patterns on the social web.

prompt: FarmVille became a Facebook gaming craze
explanation: FarmVille filled Facebook feeds with crops, gifts and requests and became one of the biggest social games of its era.

prompt: The Old Spice 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like' campaign went viral online
explanation: The campaign became a landmark example of advertising designed to spread through YouTube and social media conversation.

prompt: The 'Double Rainbow' video became a viral YouTube sensation
explanation: An ecstatic reaction to a rainbow became one of early YouTube’s most recognizable viral moments.

prompt: Nyan Cat took over the Internet
explanation: The looping pixel cat flying through space with a rainbow trail became a defining meme of early-2010s Internet culture.

prompt: Google+ launched
explanation: Google made a major attempt to challenge Facebook with Circles, Hangouts and a new social layer across its products.

prompt: Tinder launched
explanation: Tinder’s swipe interface became one of the most copied interaction patterns in mobile apps and reshaped online dating.

prompt: KONY 2012 became one of the fastest-spreading activist videos online
explanation: The campaign showed how quickly a long-form advocacy video could travel through social networks at global scale.

prompt: The Harlem Shake meme flooded YouTube
explanation: Thousands of groups copied the same short format, turning a simple template into a global participatory meme.

prompt: Doge became a breakout Internet meme
explanation: Photos of Kabosu the Shiba Inu paired with colorful Comic Sans phrases became one of the decade’s defining memes.

prompt: Twitch Plays Pokémon let a chat room control one game together
explanation: Thousands of viewers typed commands into Twitch chat to collectively play Pokémon, creating a chaotic online social experiment.

prompt: The Dress split the Internet over whether it was blue-and-black or white-and-gold
explanation: A single photo triggered a global argument about color perception and became one of the biggest viral moments of the year.

prompt: Periscope helped popularize live video from a phone
explanation: Periscope made broadcasting live video to strangers feel like a normal smartphone activity before live streaming spread across larger social platforms.

prompt: Facebook expanded Like into Reactions
explanation: Love, Haha, Wow, Sad and Angry gave billions of users more ways to react without writing a comment.

prompt: The Mannequin Challenge froze social feeds in place
explanation: Groups filmed elaborate scenes while standing perfectly still, creating an easy-to-copy viral format across social media.

prompt: HQ Trivia turned a live phone quiz into appointment viewing
explanation: Players showed up at set times to answer live trivia questions for cash prizes, briefly making a mobile game feel like live television.

prompt: The Distracted Boyfriend stock photo became a global meme template
explanation: A stock photo of a man looking back at another woman became a universal template for showing divided attention and temptation.

prompt: Yanny vs. Laurel divided the Internet over one audio clip
explanation: Millions heard the same recording differently, creating an audio version of The Dress debate.

prompt: Baby Yoda memes exploded after The Mandalorian premiered
explanation: The character later named Grogu became an immediate reaction-image and meme phenomenon across social media.

prompt: Fortnite hosted Marshmello for a huge in-game concert
explanation: The event helped establish online games as venues for large shared entertainment experiences, not just matches.

prompt: Among Us became a massive online social-deduction craze
explanation: Although released earlier, Among Us exploded during the pandemic through streamers, memes and friends playing remotely.

prompt: Clubhouse launched its invite-only audio social network
explanation: Live audio rooms briefly became one of the hottest social formats and were quickly copied by larger platforms.

prompt: Reddit traders helped turn GameStop into a global market story
explanation: WallStreetBets users became central to a dramatic surge in GameStop shares and a wider debate about online communities and finance.

prompt: Sea shanties became a TikTok craze
explanation: Collaborative duet videos turned centuries-old work songs into a surprisingly modern viral trend.

prompt: BeReal became a breakout anti-polish social app
explanation: A once-a-day notification asked friends to post simultaneously with front and rear cameras, pushing back against highly curated feeds.

prompt: Twitter was rebranded as X
explanation: The familiar blue-bird brand was replaced by X, one of the most visible platform rebrands in Internet history.

prompt: Thousands of Reddit communities went dark to protest API changes
explanation: Moderators temporarily made many subreddits private in protest over API pricing and its impact on third-party apps.
